text:
morgan: heads up - we saw 3 OOMs on serving-2 in the last 24h, all tied to kv-cache growth during very long contexts after the kernel-selector change yesterday. linking snapshots and a short log snippet below.

morgan: logs: `https://internal.s3/redwood/prod/serving-2/oom-snapshots/1719804321`

morgan: snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T21:05:12Z] OOM: kv_alloc failed size=1.2GB slab=kv_page_32
  stack: kv_alloc -> reserve_slab -> commit_page
  serving_node=serving-2-08 model=rwd-neo-13b-q8hf kernel=matmul_fused_v2 batch=8 seq_len=10240
```

devon: which model variant? only q8hf? any correlation with quant/kernel switch?

morgan: yeah all three incidents were rwd-neo-13b-q8hf but interestingly one fallback triggered q4_1 and that session kept the larger slab layout after the kernel switch -> fragmentation + growth. looks like kernel_selector picks different packing for the same logical model across warmups.

anya: I ran a quick perf profile on a repro node. notable differences:
```
kernel_selector: chosen=matmul_fused_v2 -> pad=32 -> kv_entry=48 bytes
previous: matmul_fused_v1 -> pad=16 -> kv_entry=24 bytes
result: ~2x memory per token for the same key count once the new kernel is used
```

rahul: that explains rapid growth. if the slab allocator doesn't compaction-repack on kernel transition, we end up with mixed-sized fragments that never coalesce.

jess: short-term mitigation options: enforce a per-request kv_token_limit, or disable automatic kernel switching while session has large KV, or trigger a repack on model variant switch.

morgan: can we push a canary config to limit kv cache to 64k tokens for rwd-neo variants and change eviction policy to prefer function-call boundaries? quick curl below for console canary:

morgan: `curl -XPOST https://console.redwood.internal/api/v1/configs/canary -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"filter":"model: rwd-neo-13b*","kv_limit_tokens":65536,"eviction_policy":"recency_function_marker"}'`

devon: doing that now in canary across 3 nodes in eu-west. also enabling `kernel_lock_while_long_kv=true` as an experiment.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-4521 (kv-cache OOM spikes on serving-2). Pager duty notified.

rahul: longer-term fix proposals: (1) kernel selector must emit a stable `kv_layout_version` and the runtime should detect layout mismatches and either repack on transition or ban the switch for live sessions; (2) add a background compaction pass that merges small slabs into larger contiguous pages when memory pressure detected; (3) add unit/integration test covering mixed-kernel warmup scenarios with seq_len > 8k.

jess: +1 to layout versioning. we should also record `kv_layout_version` in per-request trace so we can correlate across incidents.

morgan: assigning folks: devon -> canary rollout and kernel_lock experiment; anya -> perf repro and background compaction POC; rahul -> design doc for layout versioning + repack strategy; jess -> trace + metric work for kv_layout_version and function marker eviction telemetry.

devon: rolling canary now. will post results in ~30m. :thumbsup:

anya: repro script I used: `./tools/repro_longctx.sh --model rwd-neo-13b-q8hf --seq 11000 --mixed-fallbacks true` (this reproduces the mixed-packing behaviour in ~3 iterations).

morgan: thanks all. please keep updates here. if the canary stabilizes we can push the kv_limit temporarily cluster-wide while the engineering work proceeds.

devon: canary status 30m: no new OOMs on canary nodes, memory growth still higher but eviction policy held under control. posting detailed flame graphs to the incident ticket.

morgan: perfect. follow-ups will live in INC-4521 and the design doc PR.

jess: noted. I'll add the trace fields and a small dashboard to surface kv_layout drift.

sre-bot: INC-4521 updated - severity: prod-degraded -> mitigated (canary).

morgan: closing thread for now, will reopen if regressions appear. :white_check_mark:
